title: Tech-led upgrade campaign scripts for QBRs
summary: Draft laid out for a tech-first upgrade campaign to drive Dedicated/Private upgrades and premium SLA add-ons via QBRs and renewal paths. Includes QBR agenda script, renewal tracker columns, outreach email templates, technical validation checklist, ROI prompts, and a tentative timeline.
body:
Purpose and scope:
This doc is a working draft for a Customer Success-led, engineering-enabled upgrade motion targeting customers who are good candidates for: (1) Redwood Dedicated reserved capacity, (2) Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem) installs, and/or (3) premium SLA add-ons. It prioritizes a technical conversation anchored in QBRs and renewal windows, with clear pre-sales validation steps and an SRE/solutions handoff.

High-level qualification triggers (automated + manual):
- Sustained 95th-percentile request qps increase > 40% over 90 days
- Per-token spend exceeding $X/month (custom threshold per ARR band)
- Repeated latency SLO misses or burst patterns flagged by Observability (p95 latency or tail spikes)
- Compliance/regulatory asks captured in support tickets (PII, SOC2, HIPAA)
- Request from legal or procurement for VPC or on-prem options

QBR agenda (30–45 min technical upgrade-focused variant):
- 00:00–00:03 Quick check-in + meeting objective (CS lead)
- 00:03–00:10 Health snapshot (usage, costs, p95/p99 latency, error rate) (CS + Observability)
- 00:10–00:20 Cost economics: token economics and projection vs Dedicated (simple model) (CS)
- 00:20–00:30 Technical fit: latency profiles, KV cache/throughput behavior, quantization options, data residency ask (Eng/SE)
- 00:30–00:35 Migration approach & blockers (Solutions engineering)
- 00:35–00:40 Commercial options & timeline (AE/CS)
- 00:40–00:45 Action items and decision checkpoint (owner + due dates)

QBR script snippets (short prompts for facilitators):
- Opening: "Today we want to align on whether Dedicated or Private would give you the predictable throughput and cost profile you need for X production use cases."
- Health snapshot: "Across the last 90 days your p95 latency grew X% during peak windows — we believe Dedicated with reserved pools will reduce tail latency by ~Y% for these sequences."
- Economics: "At your current sustained throughput, our model shows a TCO reduction of ~Z% for Dedicated versus hosted pay-as-you-go; with a 12-month commit the unit cost falls further."
- Closing: "Next step: we’ll run a quick smoke test on a dedicated pool for 3 days and follow up with a migration plan and SOW draft."

Renewal/Upgrade tracker schema (CSV columns to copy into tracker):
- account_id, account_name, account_tier, current_contract_end, renewal_window_start, current_monthly_spend, 90d_avg_qps, peak_p95_latency_ms, flagged_for_upgrade (yes|no), qualified_trigger_reason, assigned_se (name), solutions_eng_involved (yes|no), proposed_offer (Dedicated|Private|SLA), commercial_owner, technical_owner, next_action, next_action_due, status_notes

Trigger-to-play mapping (decision matrix cheat sheet):
- High spend + stable traffic pattern -> Offer: Dedicated (reserved pool). Action: Cost model + 3-day dedicated smoke test + 14-day canary deployment.
- Compliance/regulatory + data residency -> Offer: Private (VPC or on-prem). Action: Kickoff security questionnaire, schedule infra workshop, estimate on-prem packaging.
- Latency tail spikes or bursty sequences + need for SLO guarantees -> Offer: Premium SLA add-on + Dedicated fallback. Action: Design fallbacks, update routing policy, document rollback plan.

Technical validation checklist (pre-SOW, engineering checklist):
- Collect heavy-hitter prompts and representative sequences (sample set with sequence lengths).
- Replay traffic subset to staging Dedicated instance; measure p50/p95/p99 and cost-per-token.
- Validate KV cache hit rates and cold-start behaviors.
- Test quantized model variants if proposed (measure quality delta on golden prompts).
- Confirm model pinning and version rollback process.
- Conduct network egress and VPC peering test (for Private).
- Security: KMS integration test, audit log verification, data retention settings.

Sample outreach email templates (short, editable):
- AE -> Technical Champion (pre-QBR):
  Subject: Quick prep for our QBR — latency & cost topics
  Body: Hi [Name], ahead of our QBR on [date], we pulled a brief snapshot showing an uptick in 95th percentile latency and spend. We want to present a Dedicated/Private option and a cost comparison that may reduce your unit costs. Can you share an example prompt set and a 1–2 person engineering contact for a short validation run?

- CS -> Exec Sponsor (renewal window):
  Subject: Renewal window + options to lower inference cost
  Body: Hi [Name], your renewal is coming up on [date]. We’ve identified a potential Dedicated reserved capacity path that could lower costs and tighten latency SLAs. Can we align on commercial guardrails and a migration pilot?

Commercial packaging suggestions (starting points):
- 12-month Dedicated commitment tiers mapped to historical spend bands; optional 30-day pilot at reduced rate for migration validation.
- Private deployment priced as platform fee + implementation hours + optional managed infra add-on.
- Premium SLA add-on (99.99% uptime + priority support) as a %-premium on monthly Dedicated fee.

Risk register (short):
- Migration risks: unexpected model incompatibility, KV cache warming causing temporary latency spikes. Mitigation: staged canary and rollback plan.
- Security risks: misconfigured VPC peering. Mitigation: checklist + security review before cutover.
- Commercial risks: price pushback. Mitigation: 30-day pilot and conservative savings projection.

Metrics to track post-upgrade (QBR followup):
- p50/p95/p99 latency improvement vs baseline
- Change in per-token unit cost
- Cache hit-rate improvement
- Number of incidents/SEV in 30/90 days post-cutover
- Customer satisfaction / NPS delta in post-migration survey

Operational handoffs (who does what):
- Customer Success: business case, QBR facilitation, commercial coordination.
- Solutions Eng: migration plan, smoke test orchestration, technical sign-off.
- SRE/Infra: capacity provisioning, network peering, monitoring config.
- Legal/Procurement: contract addendums, data residency clauses.

Open questions & TODOs (working list):
- What standard pilot price should CS offer for a 7–30 day Dedicated smoke test? (Action: CS + Finance to propose)
- Template SOW: need a minimal SOW template for Private installs (Action: Solutions Eng + Legal)
- Pre-approved list of models and quantization profiles allowed for Private deployments (Action: Applied ML)
- Sample prompts for quality regression checks (Action: Support to gather from top 10 customers)

Appendix: quick cost model primer (for CS AE to run in QBR)
- Inputs: current average tokens per month, projected growth, expected commit length, reserved pool GPU type average throughput.
- Output: estimated monthly unit cost vs hosted, expected savings percentage, rough time-to-payback.

Notes to collaborators: this is intentionally terse and engineer-forward. Add quick links to any specific customer tickets next to the account row in the tracker. Keep the tracker row updated after any validation runs. We should finalize commercial guardrails with Finance by next sprint.

Document history: first draft 2025-01-28 (Nadia Rivera). Updated 2025-02-02 with scripts and tracker schema (Liam O'Connor, Priya Nair).

Related (internal) references: CONFLUENCE-9081 (Upgrade Campaign Library), JIRA-CS-987 (Upgrade pilot backlog), github.com/redwood-inference/upgrade-scripts/pull/42 (email + qbr script templates).

---

End of draft."
